items.description: Russia continued its overnight attacks after President Volodymyr Zelensky warned of Ukraine's dwindling supplies of missile interceptors.

items.title: Saudi, Turkey, Pakistan pact comes amid US-Iran war fallout
items.description: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed a mutual defence pact on Friday that would treat any act of aggression on one of the three nations as an attack on all of them, the allies said in a joint statement. However, it did not specify if the agreement would bind them to any particular military action in each other's de…

items.title: Drones spotted in Bulgaria and Germany raise concerns of Russian escalation
items.description: The drone incidents in Europe have ignited fears that Moscow's war on Kyiv is now entangling NATO nations.

items.title: Drone enters Bulgaria, explodes near pipeline at Romanian border
items.description: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said a drone carrying a 'significant' amount of explosives exploded near the Romanian border, causing no casualties.

items.title: Deserted Or Dead? Russian Military Saves Money By Declaring Missing Soldiers AWOL
items.description: The Russian state entices men to fight in the war on Ukraine by offering high wages and relatively generous benefits. But relatives and activists say the military often avoids paying what it owes by declaring soldiers AWOL despite the likelihood that they have been killed, captured, or gone missing.

items.title: Ukraine's General Staff Reports 192 Clashes on Friday
items.description: The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 192 combat engagements as of 10 p.m. on Friday, Aug. 7, with Russian forces launching missile strikes, guided aerial bombs (KABs) and thousands of drone attacks. The Pokrovsk direction saw the most intense fighting, with 25 assaults recorded.

items.title: Iran says a shipping accord with Oman is in its final stages, but analysts warn sanctions and conflicting US and Iranian goals could limit its impact.
items.description: Iran says a shipping accord with Oman is in its final stages, but analysts warn sanctions, security concerns and rival US-Iran goals could limit its impact.

items.title: Besieged Sudanese city faces relentless drone strikes and risk of mass atrocities, U.N. warns
items.description: Hundreds of thousands of civilians in el-Obeid are being battered by relentless drone strikes and face critical water shortages and a worsening cholera outbreak, while women and girls are reporting high rates of sexual violence.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Warnings of famine and collapse as South Sudan's peace deal frays
items.description: Nearly eight million people in South Sudan – more than half the population – face crisis-level hunger, with famine risk now flagged in four counties, as the Security Council met this morning in New York. A cholera outbreak has killed more than 1,700 people, and some aid workers are being killed and abducted even as the…

items.title: ‘There were many of them, and the grass was tall’: 505 nights under Russian fire
items.description: Many soldiers in Ukraine are spending long periods on the front lines, as Ukraine struggles against Russia’s numerical advantage. One infantryman, in the trenches for nearly a year and a half straight, tells us his story.

items.title: Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign?
items.description: Russia’s online retail sector has thrived since the invasion of Ukraine. The attacks on Wildberries now threaten to disrupt that growth.
